items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: I ended up playing at Ryan’s with Roy Eldridge.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. This is like Billy Crystal’s uncle.

Oh that right. That’s it. Jesus, isn’t that terrible. Years ago I was so sharp and now I forget that sort of thing. But anyhow the point is he never lost it, Louis Armstrong. And now this gets into the definition very much, you made a good point there. You say well “Hello Dolly” time is, you know, it’s certainly not as interesting as “Struttin’ With Some Barbecue” or “Potato Head Blues,” you know, naked creativity. The situation was completely different. But he never lost his fire. He always showed something. And…

with Roy for ten, eleven years. And at the same time I was playing with Louis Armstrong. Would you believe that? Me, the immigrant’s son? Ofay Joe? You know? And I got involved between them with the deepest S-H-I-T you know. And Zutty Singleton was involved in it you know. I got Zutty and Louis Armstrong together when Zutty had a stroke. I told Louis it’s all — and remember he went to see Zutty and they hadn’t been together for years and years you know. And it was like Pops was putting down — oh he can’t play…
